Digital pianos, stage pianos, synths and MIDI controllers look alike and are set up alike. Here's what the
connections do, and how to look after them.

## Kinds of keyboard

- **Digital piano**: weighted keys, built-in speakers, mostly piano sounds. Good for practice.
- **Stage piano / workstation**: weighted or semi-weighted keys, many sounds, no speakers (needs an amp or PA).
- **Synthesizer**: sound design controls (filter, envelopes; [the Sound lessons](sound-subtractive.qmd)), usually light synth-action keys.
- **MIDI controller**: no sounds of its own. It sends MIDI to a computer or another instrument.
- **Arranger** keyboard: auto-accompaniment styles and built-in speakers.

**Key count**: 88 is a full piano; 61 and 76 are common on stage; 25–49 for controllers.

## Connections

- **Outputs**: usually **L/Mono** and **R** (1/4"). Mono gig? Use only **L/Mono**; the keyboard then sums both
  sides. Stereo: both, into two channels panned left and right, or a stereo DI.
- **Headphones**: often mutes the speakers. Turn the volume down before putting them on.
- **Sustain pedal**: plug it in **before** switching on; many keyboards read the pedal's polarity at power-up, and
  if it was plugged in later the sustain works backwards (on when lifted). Fix: switch off, plug in, switch on with
  the foot off. Or use the polarity switch on the pedal.
- **Expression pedal**: volume or other control, a separate TRS jack.
- **MIDI**: **USB** to a computer (the site's [Notation page](../tools/notation.qmd) can take a MIDI keyboard in
  Chrome), or 5-pin **MIDI Out → In** to another instrument.
- **Power**: many keyboards use a specific adaptor: wrong voltage or polarity can kill them ([Gear 1](gear-power.qmd)).

## Settings worth knowing

- **Local Off**: the keys stop playing the keyboard's own sounds and only send MIDI. Use it when the computer plays
  the sound back, or you'll hear two of everything.
- **Transpose**: shifts all keys. Easy to leave on by accident: if you sound in the wrong key, check it first.
- **Split / Layer**: two sounds on two halves, or two at once.
- **Touch / velocity curve**: lighter or heavier response.
- **Volume** slider: keep it fairly high (around ¾) and do the balance on the mixer, for less noise.

## Setup and care

- **Stand**: an X stand at a height where your forearms are level with the keys (elbows slightly above). Tighten
  every knob; check it doesn't wobble.
- **Dust cover** when not in use; no drinks on top.
- **Cleaning**: unplugged, a soft cloth very slightly damp with water (a drop of mild soap). Never spray onto the keys.
  Liquid between keys breaks contacts.
- **Moving**: a padded bag or case, keys facing your body. Don't stand it on its end without a case.
- **Cold**: a keyboard brought in from a cold car should warm up before switching on, so condensation doesn't form.
- **Sticking or dead key**: note which one and report it; don't prise keys up.
